provenance.note: Place name on the river, geocoded to the reach [supplied on this invocation]
Steady upstream discharge - the flow that carries the nutrients through the reach and sets how long the water has to grow algae in [supplied on this invocation]
Result-writing cadence; unset keeps the steering file's own period [supplied on this invocation]

Where on the reach to watch the biomass and the oxygen over time, as a Point: the pick's {coordinates, name} verbatim, a (lon, lat) pair, 'lat,lon', a point layer, or a place name. The answers are all along-reach and do not move with it [supplied on this invocation]

Modeled reach length downstream of the seed. It is also the LENGTH OF ONE PASS: the water grows algae for as long as it takes to travel this far, so a longer reach is a longer growing time [supplied on this invocation]

Simulated time. It has to cover several travel times through the reach before the along-reach answer has settled - the default is two days against a pass measured in hours. A river flushes far too fast to hold a seasonal bloom; ask a lake for that [supplied on this invocation]
Target element edge length the reach is triangulated at; it also sets the CFL time step, so it is what decides whether a long window finishes [supplied on this invocation]
Solve sizing class [declared constant default]

Phytoplankton biomass in the water entering and filling the reach - the standing crop the pass grows FROM, and what the growth ratio in the answer is held to. Stated, not fetched: `fetch_usgs_water_quality` returns chlorophyll and nutrient sample SITES, and turning scattered sites into a reach-wide field is not a step this template takes on its own [declared scenario default]

Dissolved orthophosphate entering and filling the reach - with nitrate this is what limits how much grows over the pass. Stated against the observed record from `fetch_usgs_water_quality` (characteristic 'Phosphorus'), never fetched into the deck [declared scenario default]
Non-assimilable organic phosphorus - the phosphorus locked in dead material, released back to phosphate as it breaks down. Stated [declared scenario default]

Dissolved nitrate entering and filling the reach - the other nutrient the growth is limited by. Stated against the observed record from `fetch_usgs_water_quality` (characteristic 'Nitrate') [declared scenario default]
Non-assimilable organic nitrogen - the nitrogen locked in dead material, released back to nitrate as it breaks down. Stated [declared scenario default]
Ammonium entering and filling the reach; nitrifying it is one of the things that consumes oxygen. Stated [declared scenario default]
Carbonaceous organic load (BOD) entering and filling the reach - the oxygen demand the water arrives with, before any the bloom creates for itself. Stated [declared scenario default]

Water temperature over the window. It sets the growth, mortality and nitrification rates AND the oxygen saturation the reach is measured against, so it is the single strongest lever here. Stated against the observed record from `fetch_usgs_water_quality` (characteristic 'Temperature, water'), which this run fetches over the reach and publishes beside the answer; a run coupled to the thermal process reads a computed temperature field instead and ignores this number [declared scenario default]

Solar flux at the water surface, averaged over the window. Light is what drives the growth: at zero nothing grows at all. Stated, because the engine reads this from its own keyword and from nowhere else - the atmospheric data file's radiation columns feed the thermal heat budget and never this term [declared scenario default]
The DO water-quality standard the reach is judged against; 5 is a common warm-water aquatic-life criterion [declared scenario default]
DO saturation Cs at the stated water temperature; the ceiling the oxygen is measured against [derived by trid3nt_server.workflows.telemac.helpers.water_quality.do_saturation_mgl]
Dissolved oxygen in the water entering and filling the reach; derived as saturation unless supplied [derived by trid3nt_server.workflows.telemac.helpers.water_quality.upstream_do_mgl]
not supplied; the reach flowline is fetched fresh for the AOI
not supplied; the carrier discharge is read at the MOST RECENT published NWM cycle
not supplied; the reach is solved at Strickler 33.0, which is also the roughness its outflow stage is derived as a normal depth at
not supplied; the coefficient is read as a Strickler one
not supplied; the engine's own clarity stands
